The patient was admitted to the plastic surgery service on

On ___ the patient was

The patient tolerated the OR procedures well.

Neuro: Post-operatively, the patient received Tylenol and 
oxycodone with good pain control reported.

Patient was given IV 
dilaudid for any bedside dressing changes.

CV: The patient was stable from a cardiovascular standpoint; he 
was monitored on continuous telemetry after an episode of Atrial 
fibrillation with a rapid ventricular response post-operatively 
from first OR.

This resolved with gentle hydration and vital 
signs were routinely monitored.

Telemetry was eventually 
discontinued after 5 days without arrhythmia.

He had no 
subsequent cardiovascular episodes.
Heme: Patient admitted with HCT of 25.2.

Post the first 
debridement and heavy bleeding in the OR, his HCT dropped to

He was repleted with 2 units of packed red blood cells 
and HCT rebounded to 28 and then 33.

Pulmonary: The patient was stable from a pulmonary standpoint; 
vital signs were routinely monitored.

GI/GU: Post-operatively, the patient was given IV fluids until 
tolerating oral intake.

His diet was advanced when appropriate, 
which was tolerated well.

He was also started on a bowel regimen 
to encourage bowel movement.

Foley was inserted post-operatively 
for urinary retention and then removed on hospital day #6 and 
patient able to void spontaneously.

Intake and output were 
closely monitored.

Due to unexplained anemia, ostomy contents 
were guaiac'd x 3 and were eventually found to be positive for C 
diff.
On hospital day #9, patient had 4 episodes of emesis.

KUB showed distention so a nasogastric tube was inserted and 
patient was given bowel meds.

NG tube was removed a day later 
for resolving nausea and active ostomy output.

For rest of 
hospital stay had good output from ostomy and no subsequent 
episodes of emesis.
ID: Post-operatively, the patient was given IV cefazolin Q8H x

The patient's temperature was closely watched for 
signs of infection.

Oh hospital day #10, the patient's white 
count was noted to be 21K so a UA and a C.diff were sent.

UA 
was negative but c.diff was positive.

This was converted to PO vancomycin, per ID 
recommendation, on hospital day #13.

At time of discharge his 
antibiotic plan is for 14 days total of PO vancomycin.

Urine 
culture was eventually found to positive for E coli.

However ID 
did not recommend treatment since UA was negative.

Prophylaxis: The patient received subcutaneous heparin during 
this stay, and was encouraged to get up and ambulate as much as 
possible.

His Coumadin was held during the initial admission 
period for multiple trips OR for debridement and dressing 
changes.
